name: Regolith-Choir
description: Regolith-Choir is a giant among rocky worlds, a gray colossus ringed by a shimmering band of shattered debris torn from its own crust eons ago. From high orbit the surface resolves into an endless lacework of craters overlapping craters, pale ejecta rays fanning across basins the size of nations. Its gravity, heavier than Earth's despite the airless cold, pulls a slow procession of belt asteroids into grazing passes that keep the debris ring replenished.

Standing on its surface is an exercise in humility: the horizon curves visibly away, the sky is black and crowded with the ring's glittering arc, and every step lands with the dull authority of one and a half gravities. The thin atmosphere carries nothing but the occasional hiss of electrostatic discharge as charged dust settles after solar storms. Sound dies within arm's reach, leaving travelers alone inside their own helmets in a way that some never shake.

In decaying orbits above the poles drifts a graveyard of satellites from three different wars, tumbling in silent formation around a derelict station that no fleet has ever claimed. The station's logs were wiped clean before it went dark, but its docking arms are scorched on the outside and undamaged on the inside, as if something burned away from it rather than into it. Wreck-salvagers call the whole cluster the Choir, for the harmonic interference the dead satellites broadcast when their orbits align.

Whoever controls the station controls the only intact sensor array covering the asteroid belt approaches, which is why four governments maintain quiet teams on the surface and why none of them admit it. The ring itself hides more than ice and iron: prospectors swear certain debris fragments are too regular, too machined, to be natural. The Choir keeps singing over them all, patient as only a graveyard can be, while the belt traffic grows year by year.
